t.7.96.2: O mighty-armed one, you should not grieve on my account, for such is the course of Time, bound by what was ordained long ago.
t.7.96.1: Then, seeing Rāghava with his face cast down and dejected, like the moon eclipsed, Lakṣmaṇa cheerfully spoke sweet words to him.
t.7.96.3: Kill me, gentle one, without hesitation, and keep your promise; for men who break their promises, O Kākutstha, go to hell.
t.7.96.4: If you have affection for me, O great king, if I am worthy of your favour, then slay me without hesitation and uphold dharma, O Rāghava.
t.7.96.5: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma, his senses shaken, summoned his ministers and likewise his family priest.
t.7.96.6: And in their midst the lord of men related all that had happened: the arrival of Durvāsas and also the stipulation laid down by the ascetic.
t.7.96.7: Having heard that, all the ministers, together with the preceptors, sat down; but Vasiṣṭha of great splendour spoke these words.
t.7.96.8: This has been foreseen, O mighty-armed one: your hair-raising end, and your separation from Lakṣmaṇa, O Rāma of great renown.
t.7.96.9: Abandon him, for Time is mighty; do not let your vow be made vain. For when a vow is broken, dharma itself would go to ruin.
t.7.96.10: Then, once dharma has perished, the entire three worlds, with all that moves and does not move, together with the hosts of gods and seers, would perish; of this there is no doubt.
t.7.96.11: Therefore, O tiger among men, carry out the protection of the three worlds, and by slaying Lakṣmaṇa today, make the world secure.
t.7.96.12: Having heard those words of the assembled counsellors, which were in accord with dharma and artha, Rāma, in the midst of the assembly, spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.
t.7.96.13: I banish you, Saumitri, so that there be no violation of dharma. For the virtuous, banishment or death, whichever is decreed, is one and the same.
t.7.96.14: When these words had been spoken by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, his eyes clouded with tears, departed in haste; he did not enter his own house.
t.7.96.15: Having gone to the bank of the Sarayū, he touched its water, and with joined palms, restraining all the channels of his senses, he did not let out a breath.
t.7.96.16: Then all the gods, accompanied by Śakra, with the hosts of Apsarases and the hosts of seers, showered him with flowers as he sat absorbed in yoga, no longer drawing breath.
t.7.96.18: Then the foremost of the gods, all delighted and rejoicing, together with the ṛṣis honoured the fourth portion of Viṣṇu that had arrived.
t.7.96.17: Taking hold of the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, in his very body and wholly invisible to his younger brothers, Śakra entered heaven.
